requirements.title: Identify home improvement contracts (B&P 7151.2) and apply B&P 7159

criteria: California-licensed contractor tenant using Volteira for residential customers
business_types: Licensed contractor (C-10 electrical; C-7 low voltage where held)
transaction_types: Home improvement contract

required_behavior: A 'home improvement contract' is an agreement, whether oral or written, or contained in one or more documents, between a contractor and an owner or between a contractor and a tenant (regardless of the number of units in the tenant's building, if the work is performed in, to, or upon the tenant's residence or dwelling unit), for the performance of a home improvement as defined in Section 7151, and includes all labor, services, and materials to be furnished and performed thereunder; it also includes an agreement between a salesperson and an owner or tenant for the sale, installation, or furnishing of home improvement goods or services (B&P § 7151.2).

'Home improvement' means the repairing, remodeling, altering, converting, or modernizing of, or adding to, residential property (including reconstruction, restoration, or rebuilding after a declared natural disaster), and also means the installation of home improvement goods or the furnishing of home improvement services (B&P § 7151(a)); residential electrical work for an owner or tenant falls within this definition.

For purposes of § 7159, a home improvement contract is one where the aggregate contract price specified in one or more improvement contracts, including all labor, services, and materials to be furnished by the contractor, exceeds five hundred dollars ($500) (B&P § 7159(b)); § 7159 does not apply to service and repair contracts that comply with §§ 7159.10 to 7159.14 (§ 7159(a)(2)).

Volteira must classify each job/contract (home improvement, service and repair, commercial, new construction, subcontract) and select the matching template; residential electrical work for an owner or tenant defaults to home improvement.

requirements.title: Service and repair contract: definition and qualifying conditions

criteria: Residential home improvement work for homeowner or tenant
Customer-initiated request
transaction_types: Service and repair contract
thresholds: Contract price <= $750 (verify)

required_behavior: A service and repair contract is an agreement between a contractor or salesperson for a contractor (licensed or subject to be licensed) and a homeowner or a tenant, for the performance of a home improvement as defined in § 7151, where the contract amount is seven hundred fifty dollars ($750) or less (B&P § 7159.10(a)(1)(A)).

The prospective buyer initiated contact with the contractor to request the work (§ 7159.10(a)(1)(B)); the contractor does not sell the buyer goods or services beyond those reasonably necessary to take care of the particular problem that caused the buyer to contact the contractor ((a)(1)(C)); and no payment is due, or accepted by the contractor, until the work is completed ((a)(1)(D)), meaning all of the conditions that caused the buyer to contact the contractor have been fully corrected and, if applicable, the building department has accepted and approved the corrective work ((a)(2)).

The contract must include or comply with § 7159.10(d) (in writing and signed or acknowledged, written in the same language as principally used in the oral sales presentation; legible; text in at least 10-point typeface and headings in at least 10-point boldface; signed and dated copy to the buyer before any work is started; contractor name, business address and license number; the date the contract was signed; CGL and workers' compensation notices) and § 7159.10(e) ("Service and Repair" in at least 10-point boldface; the 12-point boldface Notice to the Buyer of the four conditions, signed and dated by the buyer; "Notice to the Buyer: You are entitled to a completely filled in and signed copy of this agreement before any work may be started." in at least 12-point boldface; "Contract Price" or "Estimated Contract Price" (time and materials, with rate, materials estimate, time increments and the not-to-exceed statement); "Finance Charge" if any; "Description of the Project and Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed"; the replaced-parts statement and "OK for contractor to take replaced parts." checkbox; "Amount of Service Charge" with "You may be charged only one service charge, including any trip charge or inspection fee."; and the 12-point boldface "YOUR RIGHTS TO CANCEL BEFORE WORK BEGINS" notice, signed and dated by the buyer, five days for a senior citizen).

If any condition fails (e.g., price exceeds $750, contractor-initiated sale, or additional work raises the total above $750), § 7159.10(b) makes the home improvement contract requirements of § 7159(c), (d), and (e) applicable, including any rights to rescind under Civil Code § 1689.6 or 1689.7, regardless of the aggregate contract price; the job must be documented as a home improvement contract under B&P 7159.

Volteira may offer a service-and-repair template only when the price is <= $750, customer-initiated is recorded, and no other condition fails; change orders that push the total above $750 must convert the job to the 7159 template.

A notice with the heading "Mechanics Lien Warning" written as follows: "MECHANICS LIEN WARNING:
Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
Even if you pay your contractor in full, unpaid subcontractors, suppliers, and laborers who helped to improve your property may record mechanics liens and sue you in court to foreclose the lien. If a court finds the lien is valid, you could be forced to pay twice or have a court officer sell your home to pay the lien. Liens can also affect your credit.
To preserve their right to record a lien, each subcontractor and material supplier must provide you with a document called a 'Preliminary Notice.' This notice is not a lien. The purpose of the notice is to let you know that the person who sends you the notice has the right to record a lien on your property if they are not paid.
BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
You will not get Preliminary Notices from your prime contractor or from laborers who work on your project. The law assumes that you already know they are improving your property.
PROTECT YOURSELF FROM LIENS. You can protect yourself from liens by getting a list from your contractor of all the subcontractors and material suppliers that work on your project. Find out from your contractor when these subcontractors started work and when these suppliers delivered goods or materials. Then wait 20 days, paying attention to the Preliminary Notices you receive.
PAY WITH JOINT CHECKS. One way to protect yourself is to pay with a joint check. When your contractor tells you it is time to pay for the work of a subcontractor or supplier who has provided you with a Preliminary Notice, write a joint check payable to both the contractor and the subcontractor or material supplier.
For other ways to prevent liens, visit CSLB's internet website at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752). REMEMBER, IF YOU DO NOTHING, YOU RISK HAVING A LIEN PLACED ON YOUR HOME. This can mean that you may have to pay twice, or face the forced sale of your home to pay what you owe."

required_behavior: If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units contains a provision for arbitration of a dispute between the principals in the transaction, the provision shall be clearly titled "ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES." If included in a printed contract, it shall be set out in at least 10-point roman boldface type or in contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type, and if included in a typed contract, it shall be set out in capital letters (B&P § 7191(a)).

Immediately before the line or space provided for the parties to indicate their assent or nonassent to the arbitration provision, and immediately following it, the following shall appear (in a printed contract, in at least 10-point roman boldface type or in contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type; in a typed contract, in capital letters): "NOTICE: BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE AGREEING TO HAVE ANY DISPUTE ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE 'ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES' PROVISION DECIDED BY NEUTRAL ARBITRATION AS PROVIDED BY CALIFORNIA LAW AND YOU ARE GIVING UP ANY RIGHTS YOU MIGHT POSSESS TO HAVE THE DISPUTE LITIGATED IN A COURT OR JURY TRIAL. BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE GIVING UP YOUR JUDICIAL RIGHTS TO DISCOVERY AND APPEAL, UNLESS THOSE RIGHTS ARE SPECIFICALLY INCLUDED IN THE 'ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES' PROVISION. IF YOU REFUSE TO SUBMIT TO ARBITRATION AFTER AGREEING TO THIS PROVISION, YOU MAY BE COMPELLED TO ARBITRATE UNDER THE AUTHORITY OF THE BUSINESS AND PROFESSIONS CODE OR OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS. YOUR AGREEMENT TO THIS ARBITRATION PROVISION IS VOLUNTARY." "WE HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THE FOREGOING AND AGREE TO SUBMIT DISPUTES ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE 'ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES' PROVISION TO NEUTRAL ARBITRATION." (B&P § 7191(b)).

A provision for arbitration that does not comply with § 7191 may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee (§ 7191(c)); Volteira must require separate buyer initials and must not make arbitration a default clause without legal review.

requirements.title: Three-Day (or Five-Day) Right to Cancel notice text and 12-point boldface
requirements.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7159(e)(6)(A)-(C); Cal. Civ. Code § 1689.7(a)

criteria: Home solicitation contract or home improvement contract not negotiated at the contractor's place of business
transaction_types: Home improvement contract signed in home or remotely
thresholds: Home solicitation contract price threshold in Civ. 1689.5 (verify; historically $25)
exceptions: Contracts negotiated at the contractor's place of business (B&P 7159(e))
Valid emergency waiver (Civ. 1689.13)

required_behavior:
Provide the notice entitled "Three-Day Right to Cancel" (or "Five-Day Right to Cancel" for contracts with a senior citizen) unless the contract is negotiated at the contractor's place of business, subject to the Seven-Day Right to Cancel, or subject to the Alarm Company Act with Civil Code compliance (§ 7159(e)(6)(A)). Exact text (§ 7159(e)(6)(B)(i)): "Three-Day Right to Cancel
You, the buyer, have the right to cancel this contract within three business days. You may cancel by emailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor's place of business by midnight of the third business day after you received a signed and dated copy of the contract that includes this notice. Include your name, your address, and the date you received the signed copy of the contract and this notice.
If you cancel, the contractor must return to you anything you paid within 10 days of receiving the notice of cancellation. For your part, you must make available to the contractor at your residence, in substantially as good condition as you received them, goods delivered to you under this contract or sale. Or, you may, if you wish, comply with the contractor's instructions on how to return the goods at the contractor's expense and risk. If you do make the goods available to the contractor and the contractor does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may keep them without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the contractor, or if you agree to return the goods to the contractor and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract." References to "three" and "third" shall be changed to "five" and "fifth," respectively, for a buyer who is a senior citizen (§ 7159(e)(6)(B)(ii)).

The text of the notice is at least 12-point boldface type; the notice is in immediate proximity to a space reserved for the owner's signature; the owner acknowledges receipt of the notice by signing and dating the notice form in the signature space; and the notice is written in the same language, e.g., Spanish, as that principally used in any oral sales presentation (§ 7159(e)(6)(C)(i)-(iv)).

The notice may be attached to the contract if the contract includes, in at least 12-point boldface type, a checkbox with one of the following statements, as applicable: for a contract with a senior citizen: "The law requires that the contractor give you a notice explaining your right to cancel. Initial the checkbox if the contractor has given you a 'Notice of the Five-Day Right to Cancel.'"; for all other contracts: "The law requires that the contractor give you a notice explaining your right to cancel. Initial the checkbox if the contractor has given you a 'Notice of the Three-Day Right to Cancel.'" (§ 7159(e)(6)(C)(v)).

requirements.title: Notice of Cancellation form in duplicate, detachable
requirements.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1689.7 (verify subdivision); Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 7159(e)(6)(C)(vi)

criteria: Home solicitation contract or home improvement contract not negotiated at the contractor's place of business
transaction_types: Home improvement contract signed in home or remotely

required_behavior:
The notice shall be accompanied by a completed form in duplicate, captioned "Notice of Cancellation," which also shall be attached to the agreement or offer to purchase and be easily detachable, and which shall contain the following statement written in the same language, e.g., Spanish, as used in the contract (§ 7159(e)(6)(C)(vi)(I)): "Notice of Cancellation" / [enter date of transaction] (Date) / "You may cancel this transaction, without any penalty or obligation, within three business days from the above date.
If you cancel, any property traded in, any payments made by you under the contract or sale, and any negotiable instrument executed by you will be returned within 10 days following receipt by the seller of your cancellation notice, and any security interest arising out of the transaction will be canceled.
If you cancel, you must make available to the seller at your residence, in substantially as good condition as when received, any goods delivered to you under this contract or sale, or you may, if you wish, comply with the instructions of the seller regarding the return shipment of the goods at the seller's expense and risk.
If you do make the goods available to the seller and the seller does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may retain or dispose of the goods without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the seller, or if you agree to return the goods to the seller and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract."
To cancel this transaction, mail or deliver a signed and dated copy of this cancellation notice, or any other written notice, or send a telegram to [name of seller], at [address of seller's place of business] not later than midnight of [Date].
I hereby cancel this transaction. [Date] [Buyer's signature] The reference to "three" shall be changed to "five" for a buyer who is a senior citizen ((vi)(II)). § 7159 sets no separate type size for the form beyond the 12-point boldface rule for the text of the notice ((C)(i)) and the general 10-point minimum ((c)(2)).
For e-signed contracts, Volteira provides two copies of the form in the PDF and an electronic way to send it; legal review must confirm electronic equivalence of 'in duplicate' and 'detachable'.
